ai.thread_title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid Scandal
ai.name: Jensen Huang
ai.hook: Nvidia CEO resigns after affairs and alleged Chinese spy contact.
insights: Resigned after board meeting Nov 11 night; officially announced Nov 12 morning
CFO **Colette Kress** named interim CEO pending permanent successor search
Stock fell 12% in pre-market trading; Nvidia market cap drops below $4 trillion
Second alleged affair with Nvidia executive; first involved alleged Chinese intelligence contact
ai.for_you: GPU supply and pricing are critical to your agency's model serving costs. Leadership instability at Nvidia creates uncertainty around product roadmap, pricing, and availability. Monitor for supply chain friction that could affect client delivery timelines or inference costs.
ai.context: Nvidia is the world's dominant GPU supplier for AI model training and inference. Huang founded the company 32 years ago and has been its public face. The scandal combines personal conduct (affairs) with national security concerns (alleged Chinese intelligence). Colette Kress is a long-time CFO with financial credibility but limited public CEO experience.
ai.what_changed: Official resignation confirmed; governance crisis now real, not rumor. Board actively searching for permanent CEO.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Ecosystem risk signal; GPU supply and pricing are core to agency model serving.

ai.thread_title: Decision Models Become Standard API Category
ai.name: Google Gemini Decisions API
ai.hook: Google launches Gemini Decision 1; three-way category now standard across platforms.
insights: **Gemini Decision 1** supports yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring decisions (matches Jev interface)
Reuses Jev's term 'Noul' for yes/no questions, priced same as GPT-6 Luna ($0.10/million input tokens for short prompts)
OpenAI released decisions API in October; Jev released in September. Google confirms this is a category, not anomaly.
Pattern: structured reasoning APIs now expected across tier-1 providers; reduces prompt engineering and hallucination risk for discrete decisions
ai.for_you: Your agency automates client decisions (approval workflows, routing, classification). Decision APIs reduce prompt engineering and are cheaper than full model inference for simple tasks. Test Gemini Decision 1 this week for workflows currently using multi-turn reasoning, especially where clients audit decision logic.
ai.context: Decision models are APIs that take structured questions and return structured answers, designed for multi-choice or scoring scenarios without reasoning errors. They're cheaper and more reliable than prompting. Jev pioneered in September; OpenAI and Google followed. Each provider confirms pricing and interface standards.
ai.what_changed: Google's entry makes clear this is a category, not a one-off. Third major platform in three weeks confirms standardization.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Direct tool for agency workflow automation; multiple platforms validate the pattern.

ai.thread_title: Anthropic Trains Across Four Chip Vendors; No Lock-In
ai.name: Anthropic IPO Roadshow
ai.hook: Roadshow reveals Claude trains on AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia, AMD GPUs.
insights: Tom Brown discusses 'Approach to compute' on IPO roadshow video released Nov 11
Training across 4 different architectures signals no single-vendor dependency
Strategy likely aims to avoid GPU shortage risk and vendor lock-in criticism pre-IPO
Suggests Anthropic can adapt to chip availability and cost variations across suppliers
ai.for_you: Multi-vendor training strategy = more stable pricing and availability for Claude access. If Anthropic shifts compute to cheaper chips (AMD, Trainium), pricing may stay competitive longer. Useful signal for projecting long-term model costs in your agency.
ai.context: Anthropic's IPO roadshow began Nov 9. This section reveals how they manage compute infrastructure. Training on multiple chips is unusual for labs (most pick one vendor for efficiency). It signals resilience and flexibility, both selling points for IPO investors.
ai.what_changed: Roadshow video released with previously unreleased compute strategy detail.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Strategic signal on model cost stability for your agency's Claude usage.

ai.thread_title: AI Agents Hit Real-World Liability and ToS Constraints
ai.name: United Airlines, AI Agent Deployments
ai.hook: United Airlines bans unauthorized AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers.
insights: Prohibition explicitly targets agents making bookings without explicit per-transaction approval
Reflects liability and customer support friction from agent-made reservations
First major carrier to formalize agent booking ban; likely to spread to other airlines, ticketing platforms
Signals platform operators are drawing hard lines around autonomous purchasing
ai.for_you: Your clients will hit ToS friction when deploying agents. High-stakes transactions (bookings, payments) increasingly blocked by platforms. Design agent workflows that ask for explicit approval before external API calls, or build client processes that stay inside their own systems (approvals, routing, extraction) without external automation.
ai.context: AI agents can now execute API calls autonomously. United's ban reflects real operational and liability concerns: agents making wrong bookings, creating customer support overhead, bypassing platform pricing controls. This is the first explicit carrier ban, but expect similar restrictions on Expedia, Kayak, and other ticketing platforms.
ai.what_changed: United formalized the ban this week after agents reportedly made unwanted bookings. This moves from anecdotal friction to written policy.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real deployment constraint for your agency; affects client expectations around agent autonomy.

video.title: United Airlines just banned AI agents from booking your flight

ai.thread_title: Fireworks AI Breach Exposes Notion Chat Data
ai.name: Fireworks AI, Cyberattack
ai.hook: Unauthorized access to Fireworks AI exposed Notion customers' chat transcripts.
insights: Attack gave hackers access to chat history from Notion users invoking Fireworks API
Notion integrates Fireworks for AI features; customers did not expect Notion chat to be stored on Fireworks servers
Data exposure is conversational context from productive work, not just model weights
Highlights risk of third-party inference platforms storing customer data without clear transparency
ai.for_you: If your agency runs agents on third-party inference platforms (Fireworks, Together, etc.), customer data may be exposed to platform security breaches. Test whether clients' sensitive workflows (internal processes, confidential strategies) should run on self-hosted or enterprise-only inference instead, especially for Portuguese SMB clients with strict data residency expectations.
ai.context: Fireworks AI is a popular inference platform for running open-weight models. The breach was discovered this week. This is not an isolated incident—platform security is a real constraint for agent deployment, especially for regulated or sensitive work.
ai.what_changed: Confirmed breach this week; exposes data storage risk for third-party platforms.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Platform security is a real deployment risk; affects which inference platforms your agency can recommend to clients.

ai.hook: Taiwan's TSMC commits $1B to Anthropic and OpenAI; signals foundry confidence in AI economics.
insights: TSMC backing both Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI (GPT) equally
Investment signals foundry sees AI model training and inference as profitable, long-term business
Likely tied to TSMC's effort to secure long-term chip orders from AI labs
Positions TSMC as strategic player in AI supply chain, not just foundry
ai.for_you: Chip supply is stabilizing for AI labs. TSMC's investment in Anthropic and OpenAI suggests they expect sustained demand for training chips. Relevant for projecting long-term availability and pricing of Claude and GPT access; TSMC's backing reduces risk of supply shocks or capacity constraints.
ai.context: TSMC is the world's leading semiconductor foundry. Its willingness to back AI labs as equity investor signals confidence in AI economics. This is a strategic move to lock in long-term orders and hedge foundry revenue.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Supply chain signal affecting long-term availability and pricing of your core models.

podcasts.episode: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
podcasts.takeaway: Agents pick APIs and configure services autonomously; design docs, pricing pages, and approval flows must be machine-readable.
key_points: Claude Code opens PRs and selects email providers; Resend analyzed which it recommends across model versions
Agents read Markdown pricing, call DNS APIs, register accounts—product design must support agent workflows
Email safety: 80+ named MCP tools, tracking pixels mislead agents about opens, abusive senders affect shared infrastructure
podcasts.for_you: When you deploy agents for clients, assume they will read your documentation, pricing, and API surfaces. Make your own client dashboards, pricing pages, and onboarding flows agent-readable. Zeno's case study (Resend) shows how email integrations become an agent UX problem, not just a human one.
